# Objective

Implement G9O1 deterministic source/knowledge bundles and operational guide
hardening on `feature/g9o1-source-knowledge-bundles-guides`.

**AUTHORIZED CANONICAL PROMPT — NOT STARTED / UNEXECUTED.**

# Mandatory entry gate

Require G9P author approval, approved normative bundle/documentation specs,
Accepted ADR 0015, clean branch from the approved G9P commit/tag, recorded
prompt hash, and green operational/composed authority. Author closeout
authorized G9O1, but this file does not execute it; an explicit canonical task
invocation is still required.

# Hard dependencies

Approved G9P operations/documentation contracts and repository provenance are
hard contract inputs. No spatial, Locus, DXF or workspace phase is a semantic
dependency of G9O1.

# Recommended execution predecessor

Execute G9O1 first after final G9P approval so every later phase can consume
reproducible guides and bounded context. This is an operational recommendation,
not a semantic edge into G9A1.

# Global/release gate

Fresh deterministic G9O1 evidence is required by the integrated G9 operational
closeout, but failure here cannot be reported as undefined spatial mathematics.

# Authority and evidence hierarchy

Read current Git/build/catalog/licensing source, `AGENTS.md`, approved G9P
operations contracts, then architecture and characterization evidence.

# Scope

Implement the checked-in generator under `tools/knowledge`, configured profiles,
manifest/schema validation, deterministic archive/text chunks, rights-aware
exclusions, clean/explicit-dirty modes, guide hardening, tests and evidence.

# Explicitly forbidden scope

No spatial/Locus/DXF/GUI semantics, no unrestricted filesystem crawl, no
restricted binary inclusion by default, no generated bundle committed to Git,
and no execution of later prompts.

# Editable boundaries

`tools/knowledge`, operations specs/config/schema, agent verifiers, relevant
guides/architecture/validation, and ignored `artifacts/knowledge` only.

# Productive versus test-private permissions

Productive generator and operational docs are allowed within scope. Probes must
be deterministic fixtures and cannot weaken exclusions or provenance.

# Architectural placement

Bundle creation is operational tooling. It enumerates the Git index and reads
authoritative source; it is not an application or kernel runtime feature.

# Required design/specification

Implement only the approved ownership precedence, profiles, manifest, hashing,
chunking, path safety, budgets, freshness, dirty-tree, and rights contracts.

# Geometric invariants and degeneracies

Bundles preserve source boundaries and authority metadata; they never flatten
or reinterpret geometric semantics.

# Compatibility and serialization

Bundle schemas are versioned. Historical evidence and raw binary bytes remain
unchanged; text normalization applies only where declared.

# Required tests and commands

Test byte-equal reruns, profile membership, ownership precedence, raw/canonical
hashes, clean/dirty state, exclusions, path traversal/symlinks, budgets and
freshness. Run the focused G9O1 verifier and `tools/agent/verify.ps1` without
`-SkipBuild`.

# Required artifacts

Generator, fixtures/tests, focused verifier, machine evidence, guide updates,
traceability and phase report.

# Stop conditions

Stop if ownership is ambiguous, output is nondeterministic, restricted content
enters by default, paths escape the repository, source authority is lost, or
an operational failure is misrepresented as a geometric dependency.
